copy.normal: Hercul sees your CNS load running {cns.acwr|1dp}× your four-week average. That is the point where progress starts costing more than it returns — take a deload week.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {cns.acwr|1dp}× your four-week average and no deload in sight. You are not being hard, you are being slow. Take the week.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your CNS is running high today — readiness {cns.readiness|pct}%. Good day for isolations. Push the heavy compounds to your next session.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {cns.readiness|pct}% readiness. Whatever heroic compound you had planned today, it is going to be a bad rep at a weight you already own. Do isolations.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you fully recovered — readiness {cns.readiness|pct}%. This is the day to go after a top set.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {cns.readiness|pct}% readiness. No excuses available today. Go and be heavy.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} chest sets and {volume.weeklySets:Rear Delts|int} rear delt sets this week. If your shoulders complain on bench, that ratio is the first place to look.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} sets of chest and {volume.weeklySets:Rear Delts|int} of rear delts. Then you wonder why your shoulders hurt on bench. That is not bad luck, that is arithmetic.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {volume.pushPct|int}% of your volume going to pushing. Pulling builds the shoulders that let you keep pushing — even it up over the next few weeks.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {volume.pushPct|int}% push. You are building the half of your body you can see in the mirror and quietly skipping the half that holds it together.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Quads|int} quad sets against {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} for chest this week. Legs carry everything else — give them a real session.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Quads|int} sets of quads. Your upper body is thriving and your legs have been quietly retired. Hercul is not angry, just disappointed.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} chest sets this week — past the point most people can recover from. More is not the missing ingredient here.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} chest sets. You are not training chest any more, you are just visiting it repeatedly.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you hitting {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% of your protein target this week across {session.sessionsThisWeek|int} sessions. You are training hard enough to deserve the recovery — one more solid portion a day covers it.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {session.sessionsThisWeek|int} sessions this week and {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% of your protein target. You are paying for the gym and refusing to collect.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you averaging {nutrition.kcalPct7d|pct}% of your calorie target while cutting. The target is the plan — either eat to it or move it deliberately.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {nutrition.kcalPct7d|pct}% of your calorie target on a cut. That is not a cut, that is maintenance with extra paperwork.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {nutrition.kcalPct7d|pct}% of your calorie target while you are trying to gain. Muscle is built from surplus, not from good intentions.
copy.honest: Hercul sees you trying to grow on {nutrition.kcalPct7d|pct}% of your target. You cannot build a house and skip the bricks.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {nutrition.daysLogged7d|int} days logged out of seven. He is not going to draw conclusions from that — and neither should you.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {nutrition.daysLogged7d|int} days logged this week. Hard to fix a diet nobody is willing to look at.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% of your protein target, six days logged. This is the boring part that actually works. Keep it.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% protein and a full week logged. Fine. Hercul has nothing to complain about. Do not let it go to your head.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your weight has moved {body.weightDeltaKg:21|abs} kg in three weeks while you are cutting. Nothing is broken — the intake just is not where you think it is. Re-weigh portions for a week or take another 200 kcal off.
copy.honest: Hercul sees three weeks of cutting and {body.weightDeltaKg:21|abs} kg to show for it. Something is not making it into the log. Hercul is not angry, just disappointed.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your bodyweight flat over three weeks on a gaining phase. Add 200 kcal and hold it for a fortnight before judging it.
copy.honest: Hercul sees three weeks of "bulking" and no bulk. You are eating like someone who is scared of the scale.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg down in two weeks. That is faster than muscle survives — ease the deficit unless there is a reason for the hurry.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg gone in a fortnight. Some of that was muscle you spent a year earning. Slow down.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {exercise.lastPerformedDays:barbell-back-squat|int} days since your last squat, while everything else is on schedule. Put it back at the front of a session.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {exercise.lastPerformedDays:barbell-back-squat|int} days since you squatted. Everything else is going great. Funny, that.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {session.daysSinceLastWorkout|int} days since your last session. Do not try to make it up — just do a normal workout today.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {session.daysSinceLastWorkout|int} days. The plan does not care why. Go and do a session, an ordinary one, today.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {session.sessionsPerWeek4w|1dp} sessions a week for a month straight. That consistency is worth more than any single programme.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {session.sessionsPerWeek4w|1dp} sessions a week for four weeks. Hercul has checked twice and can find nothing wrong. Unsettling.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you squatting regularly at {profile.heightCm|int} cm. Longer femurs force more forward lean to keep the bar over midfoot, so a low-bar position or a heeled shoe usually buys back the depth you are fighting for. Worth a three-week trial.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {profile.heightCm|int} cm grinding high-bar squats. Your femurs are never going to make that look like the video. Go low-bar or put your heels up — it is leverage, not character.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your sumo deadlift sitting at {exercise.e1rmRatio:sumo-deadlift:barbell-back-squat|1dp}× your back squat. At {profile.heightCm|int} cm that is largely anatomy — a wide stance asks a lot of long femurs. Conventional often suits your build better; run it for a block and compare.
copy.honest: Hercul sees your sumo barely clearing your squat at {exercise.e1rmRatio:sumo-deadlift:barbell-back-squat|1dp}×. Some of that is being {profile.heightCm|int} cm and pulling the stance that punishes it. Pick conventional, commit to a block, then argue.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you benching often at {profile.heightCm|int} cm on {volume.weeklySets:Rear Delts|int} rear delt sets a week. Long arms mean a longer bar path and more triceps off the chest, and the shoulder spends longer at end range — direct rear delt and rotator work is part of the lift, not an extra.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {profile.heightCm|int} cm of leverage against you on bench and {volume.weeklySets:Rear Delts|int} rear delt sets defending the joint. Long arms make that press a shoulder-health problem before it is a chest problem. Fix the back of the shoulder.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you pulling conventional at {profile.heightCm|int} cm — a shorter build usually keeps the bar close and the back angle friendly here. Worth trying a heavier top set before assuming sumo is the answer.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {profile.heightCm|int} cm pulling conventional. That is the stance your build is actually good at. Stop reading about sumo and add weight.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you up {body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg over two weeks while logging a deficit. Unless you have just started creatine, which holds water, some calories are going unlogged — oils and snacks are the usual suspects.
copy.honest: Hercul sees +{body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg on the scale and a deficit in the app. Unless you are drinking creatine by the spoonful, you are eating food you are not logging. The math does not lie.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you logging a surplus while the scale dropped {body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg. Your real expenditure is running higher than the estimate — add food if you want to grow.
copy.honest: You log a bulk, the scale says -{body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg. Stop eating like a bird and eat an actual surplus.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you in a surplus with a squat that has not moved in 14 days. Those extra calories are not turning into muscle — check your training volume, or sleep more.
copy.honest: Hercul sees a surplus and a squat that has not moved in 14 days. You are not bulking, you are just eating. Add volume or add sleep, then earn the food.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your strength climbing through a deficit. That is fatigue management and programming done right — keep it exactly as it is.
copy.honest: Strength up while in a deficit. That is the hard version and you are pulling it off. Do not get clever and change something.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you squat {exercise.e1rmRatioBelted:barbell-back-squat|1dp}x more with a belt than without. Your legs clearly have the strength; your core is what is holding them back — start on dedicated trunk work (planks, ab wheel).
copy.honest: Your belted squat is {exercise.e1rmRatioBelted:barbell-back-squat|1dp}x your raw squat. The belt is doing your abs' job. Fix the core, or your back pays for it.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your sleep tracking closely with your training RPE. After a bad night, expect the same weights to feel heavier today — plan around it rather than pushing through.
copy.honest: Your RPE follows your sleep almost one to one. You slept badly, so today's weights will feel heavy, and that is not a lack of grit. Do not run into the wall to prove a point.

copy.normal: Hercul noticed you have relatively long femurs. For your upcoming squats, you might find a low-bar position or an elevated heel more comfortable to maintain an upright torso.
copy.honest: Hercul sees you've got long femurs and a squat coming up. If you're doing high-bar in flat shoes, you're fighting your own mechanics. Try low-bar or lifting shoes.

copy.normal: With a longer arm span, bench pressing requires a greater range of motion. Consider a slightly wider grip to reduce shoulder strain at the bottom.
copy.honest: Long arms mean you have to press the bar an extra mile. Widen your grip a bit or you're just putting unnecessary wear on your shoulders.

copy.normal: Hercul sees the scale up +{body.weightDeltaKg:1|1dp} kg after {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of carbs before bed. Each gram of stored glycogen binds ~3 g of intracellular water — that jump is muscle fullness, not adipose tissue. Use the extra leverage on today's heavy sets.
copy.honest: Scale jumped +{body.weightDeltaKg:1|1dp} kg after {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of late-night carbs and you are already panicking. One gram of glycogen holds three grams of water inside the muscle. Put the calculator away and go lift.

copy.normal: Hercul sees +{body.weightDeltaKg:3|1dp} kg over three days alongside {nutrition.carbsYesterdayG|int} g of carbohydrates yesterday. Replenished muscle glycogen and bound intracellular water explain the rise — expect fuller muscles and stronger rep endurance today.
copy.honest: You ate {nutrition.carbsYesterdayG|int} g of carbs and the scale moved +{body.weightDeltaKg:3|1dp} kg in three days. That is refilled glycogen and water inside the muscle belly, not tissue gain. Channel it into the bar.

copy.normal: Hercul sees a {body.weightDeltaKg:1|abs} kg overnight drop after only {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of evening carbs. Lower overnight glycogen releases bound water, so your morning weight sits at the bottom of your hydration band.
copy.honest: Down {body.weightDeltaKg:1|abs} kg overnight because you ate {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of carbs before bed. That is drained glycogen water, not a miracle overnight cut. Eat some carbs before you train.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your lifting loads up +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}% following {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of evening carbs. Overnight muscle glycogen storage directly fuels morning and afternoon bar velocity — keep this pre-training night protocol.
copy.honest: Lifting weights are up +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}% after {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of carbs before bed. Turns out stocked muscle glycogen moves more iron than willpower alone. Repeat it.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your lifting weights down {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% after logging only {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of evening carbs. Going to bed glycogen-depleted leaves muscles flat and cuts 8–12 rep output — shift 60–80 g of carbs to dinner before blaming your programme.
copy.honest: Your working weights dropped {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% after {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of evening carbs. You showed up to lift with an empty tank and acted surprised when the bar felt bolted to the floor. Eat carbs at dinner.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of evening carbs paired with {biometrics.sleepYesterdayHours|1dp} h of sleep and {cns.readiness|pct}% CNS readiness. Evening carbohydrates lower nocturnal cortisol and support sleep architecture — your regeneration is primed.
copy.honest: {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of carbs before bed, {biometrics.sleepYesterdayHours|1dp} h of sleep, and {cns.readiness|pct}% CNS readiness. You accidentally executed textbook recovery physiology.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your scale weight up +{body.weightDeltaKg:7|1dp} kg this week while saturating creatine ({supplements.creatineDays7d|int}/7 days). Creatine osmotically pulls 0.8–2.0 kg of water inside the muscle cell — this is beneficial lean cell volume that boosts strength, not unwanted gain.
copy.honest: You started taking creatine ({supplements.creatineDays7d|int}/7 days) and the scale went up +{body.weightDeltaKg:7|1dp} kg. That water is inside your muscle fibers where you want it. Do not touch your calories.

copy.normal: Hercul sees +{body.weightDeltaKg:14|1dp} kg over 14 days despite controlled calories ({nutrition.kcalPct14d|pct}% of target), alongside {supplements.creatineDays14d|int}/14 days of creatine. Intracellular muscle hydration explains the scale offset.
copy.honest: Scale says +{body.weightDeltaKg:14|1dp} kg on {nutrition.kcalPct14d|pct}% calories because you took creatine {supplements.creatineDays14d|int} of the last 14 days. Your muscles are holding intracellular water. That is the whole point of taking it.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your weight down {body.weightDeltaKg:7|abs} kg this week while creatine intake dropped to {supplements.creatineDays7d|int}/7 days. Skipping creatine releases intracellular muscle water, lowering scale weight and reducing muscle fullness.
copy.honest: Down {body.weightDeltaKg:7|abs} kg this week and only {supplements.creatineDays7d|int}/7 days of creatine logged. Half of that drop is intracellular water leaving your muscles because you forgot your scoop.

copy.normal: Hercul sees lifting loads up +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}% with {supplements.creatineDays7d|int}/7 days of creatine saturation. Saturated phosphocreatine pools speed up ATP regeneration between heavy sets — your consistency is paying off on the bar.
copy.honest: {supplements.creatineDays7d|int}/7 days of creatine and working weights up +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}%. Full phosphocreatine stores buy you the extra rep at the end of a heavy set. Keep taking it.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your working weights down {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% alongside {supplements.creatineDays7d|int}/7 days of creatine this week. Lower intramuscular phosphocreatine and reduced sarcoplasmic hydration shave 1–2 reps off heavy sets — resume daily dosing.
copy.honest: Lifting loads dipped {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% and you only took creatine {supplements.creatineDays7d|int} times this week. You drained your ATP buffer and lost intracellular leverage. Take the scoop daily.

copy.normal: Hercul sees creatine missed yesterday ({supplements.creatineDays7d|int}/7 days this week). Daily saturation keeps intracellular hydration and top-set ATP recovery steady — log today's dose.
copy.honest: {supplements.creatineDays7d|int}/7 days of creatine and missed again yesterday. Creatine works by saturation, not by occasional cameo appearances.

copy.normal: Hercul sees saturated creatine ({supplements.creatineDays7d|int}/7d) combined with {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of evening carbs. Intracellular muscle hydration and glycogen are both maxed out — expect peak joint cushioning and pressing leverage today.
copy.honest: Saturated creatine plus {nutrition.carbsBeforeBedYesterdayG|int} g of late carbs means your muscle cells are maximally hydrated today. If you cannot hit a good top set today, it is not the fuel.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your scale down {body.weightDeltaKg:1|abs} kg after a {fasting.yesterdayHours|1dp} h fast. Fasting lowers insulin and releases liver/muscle glycogen along with bound water and sodium — expect 0.4–1.0 kg to return normally when you refeed.
copy.honest: You fasted {fasting.yesterdayHours|1dp} hours and the scale dropped {body.weightDeltaKg:1|abs} kg. Most of that is flushed glycogen water and gut weight, so do not lose your mind when half of it comes back after dinner.

copy.normal: Hercul sees a +{body.weightDeltaKg:1|1dp} kg scale bounce after breaking your {fasting.yesterdayHours|1dp} h fast with {nutrition.carbsYesterdayG|int} g of carbs. Refilling depleted glycogen supercompensates intracellular water — this is normal physiological restoration.
copy.honest: Scale bounced +{body.weightDeltaKg:1|1dp} kg after breaking a {fasting.yesterdayHours|1dp} h fast with {nutrition.carbsYesterdayG|int} g of carbs. That is water rushing back into empty muscle glycogen stores, not overnight tissue gain.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your lifting weights down {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% alongside a {fasting.yesterdayHours|1dp} h fast. Extended fasting reduces intramuscular glycogen and raises cortisol during multi-set volume work — schedule a carb+protein meal 60–90 minutes before heavy sessions.
copy.honest: Your working weights dropped {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% after fasting {fasting.yesterdayHours|1dp} hours. Glycolytic sets of 8–12 run on glycogen, not vibes. Break the fast before heavy lifting or accept the lighter bar.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you {fasting.activeHours|1dp} h into an active fast with CNS load already elevated ({cns.readiness|pct}% readiness). Training heavy compounds in a deep fasted state compounds cortisol and delays muscle regeneration — refeed first or keep today's session light.
copy.honest: You are {fasting.activeHours|1dp} hours fasted with {cns.readiness|pct}% CNS readiness. Maxing out before eating today is a recipe for catabolism and a missed rep. Eat first or dial back the load.

copy.normal: Hercul sees a {fasting.yesterdayHours|1dp} h fasting window compressing your feeding time, leaving protein at {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% of target. Fasting only preserves lean mass if full daily protein is hit inside the eating window.
copy.honest: Fasting {fasting.yesterdayHours|1dp} hours is costing you your protein target ({nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}%). A shorter eating window is not an excuse to under-recover your muscles.

copy.normal: Hercul sees a {fasting.yesterdayHours|1dp} h fast paired with {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% protein adherence and steady lifting loads (+{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}%). You are getting insulin-sensitivity and autophagy benefits without sacrificing strength.
copy.honest: {fasting.yesterdayHours|1dp} h fast, {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% protein, and lifting numbers holding strong. That is how intermittent fasting is supposed to be run.

copy.normal: Hercul sees lifting loads down {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% after {nutrition.alcoholYesterdayDrinks|1dp} drinks ({nutrition.alcoholYesterdayG|int} g ethanol) yesterday. Alcohol impairs CNS motor unit recruitment, dehydrates muscle fibers, and blunts protein synthesis by ~24% — treat today as a recovery session.
copy.honest: Working weights dropped {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% the day after {nutrition.alcoholYesterdayDrinks|1dp} drinks. Ethanol taxes your central nervous system and steals your REM sleep. Do not blame the programme for last night's tab.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your session RPE averaging {workout.lastSessionAvgRpe|1dp} following {nutrition.alcoholYesterdayDrinks|1dp} drinks yesterday. Post-alcohol dehydration and reduced neural drive inflate perceived effort by 1–1.5 RPE at the same bar weight.
copy.honest: Session RPE hit {workout.lastSessionAvgRpe|1dp} after {nutrition.alcoholYesterdayDrinks|1dp} drinks yesterday. The weights did not get heavier; your nervous system is just hungover. Leave a rep in the tank today.

copy.normal: Hercul sees the scale up +{body.weightDeltaKg:1|1dp} kg after {nutrition.alcoholYesterdayDrinks|1dp} drinks yesterday. After alcohol's initial diuretic effect wears off, rebound cortisol and aldosterone cause extracellular water retention for 24–48 h. Hydrate with electrolytes to flush it.
copy.honest: Up +{body.weightDeltaKg:1|1dp} kg the day after {nutrition.alcoholYesterdayDrinks|1dp} drinks. That is cortisol and aldosterone holding extracellular water while your liver clears acetate. Drink three litres of water and skip the crash-diet panic.

copy.normal: Hercul sees a {body.weightDeltaKg:1|abs} kg scale drop the morning after {nutrition.alcoholYesterdayDrinks|1dp} drinks. Alcohol suppresses vasopressin (ADH), flushing body water — rehydrate with 750 ml water and electrolytes before training so joints and strength are protected.
copy.honest: Scale dropped {body.weightDeltaKg:1|abs} kg after {nutrition.alcoholYesterdayDrinks|1dp} drinks yesterday. You did not diet in your sleep; you are dehydrated. Drink water and salt before you touch a barbell.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {nutrition.alcoholYesterdayG|int} g of alcohol yesterday stacked on {cns.readiness|pct}% CNS readiness. Alcohol suppresses mTOR signaling and overnight growth hormone pulses — prioritize hydration, protein, and sub-maximal RPE 7 work today.
copy.honest: {nutrition.alcoholYesterdayG|int} g of alcohol yesterday while CNS readiness sits at {cns.readiness|pct}%. Your muscle regeneration is running at a discount today. Keep the ego out of the rack.

copy.normal: Hercul sees alcohol logged on {nutrition.alcoholDays7d|int} of the last 7 days. Frequent intake chronically elevates cortisol, masks scale progress with extracellular water, and blunts weekly strength adaptation.
copy.honest: Alcohol on {nutrition.alcoholDays7d|int} days this week. You are training to build muscle all afternoon and pouring recovery suppressant on it at night. Pick which goal is actually driving.

copy.normal: Hercul sees +{body.weightDeltaKg:1|1dp} kg on the scale after {nutrition.sodiumYesterdayMg|int} mg of sodium yesterday. High plasma osmolarity holds transient extracellular water for 24–48 h, which also cushions joints and boosts gym pumps today.
copy.honest: You ate {nutrition.sodiumYesterdayMg|int} mg of sodium yesterday and gained +{body.weightDeltaKg:1|1dp} kg of water overnight. Drink water, enjoy the absurd bench pump today, and watch it flush out tomorrow.

copy.normal: Hercul sees lifting loads down {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% with only {nutrition.waterYesterdayMl|int} ml of water logged yesterday. Even a 2% drop in cellular hydration reduces barbell force output by 5–8% — drink 600 ml before your warmup.
copy.honest: Only {nutrition.waterYesterdayMl|int} ml of water yesterday and your lifts dropped {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}%. Dehydrated muscle fibers contract poorly. Drink water before you blame your strength.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {nutrition.waterYesterdayMl|int} ml of hydration yesterday supporting a +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}% climb in lifting loads. High cellular hydration keeps plasma volume and muscle leverage at their peak.
copy.honest: {nutrition.waterYesterdayMl|int} ml of water logged and lifting weights up +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}%. Proper hydration is the cheapest performance enhancer in the gym.

copy.normal: Hercul sees lifting performance down {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% after {biometrics.sleepYesterdayHours|1dp} h of sleep. Short sleep slows glycogen replenishment and reduces high-threshold motor unit firing — cap sets at RPE 8 today.
copy.honest: {biometrics.sleepYesterdayHours|1dp} hours of sleep and your lifts dipped {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}%. Sleep debt taxes bar speed first. Get to bed on time tonight instead of grinding sloppy reps.

copy.normal: Hercul sees +{body.weightDeltaKg:1|1dp} kg on the scale after {biometrics.sleepYesterdayHours|1dp} h of sleep. Sleep restriction elevates morning cortisol, which holds extracellular fluid and masks real body composition progress.
copy.honest: Slept {biometrics.sleepYesterdayHours|1dp} hours and the scale ticked up +{body.weightDeltaKg:1|1dp} kg. High morning cortisol from sleep debt holds water. One full night of sleep flushes it.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {biometrics.sleepAvg7dHours|1dp} h average sleep this week driving a +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}% surge in lifting loads. Deep and REM sleep are where neural adaptations lock in.
copy.honest: Averaging {biometrics.sleepAvg7dHours|1dp} hours of sleep and lifting weights are up +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}%. Sleep is still undefeated.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your 14-day bodyweight essentially flat ({body.weightDeltaKg:14|1dp} kg) while lifting loads climbed +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}%. Rising strength at stable bodyweight is the textbook signature of body recomposition.
copy.honest: Scale barely moved ({body.weightDeltaKg:14|1dp} kg in 14d) while lifting weights jumped +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}%. You are replacing stored tissue with contractile muscle. Stop staring only at the scale.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you down {body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg over 14 days while lifting loads held or climbed (+{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}%). Maintaining bar weight during a cut confirms your lean muscle mass is protected.
copy.honest: Down {body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg in two weeks and lifting numbers are up +{workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|1dp}%. Zero muscle lost. Keep the deficit and protein right where they are.

copy.normal: Hercul sees lifting loads down {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}% alongside a {body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg 14-day drop. Glycogen depletion and an aggressive deficit are taxing your top sets — place your daily carbs around training and before bed to defend bar weight.
copy.honest: Down {body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg in 14 days and your lifting weights crashed {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}%. If you let bar weight free-fall on a cut, your body has no reason to keep the muscle. Time your carbs around training.

copy.normal: Hercul sees bodyweight up +{body.weightDeltaKg:14|1dp} kg over 14 days while lifting loads dipped {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}%. When scale weight rises without bar progression, accumulated CNS fatigue, poor sleep, or alcohol is blocking hypertrophy.
copy.honest: Scale is up +{body.weightDeltaKg:14|1dp} kg on a bulk, but your lifting weights are down {workout.liftingDeltaPct7d|abs}%. Extra calories without progressive overload or recovery do not build muscle. Check your sleep and CNS load.

copy.normal: Hercul sees a high water retention index (+{biometrics.waterRetentionIndex|int}) coinciding with a +{body.weightDeltaKg:3|1dp} kg 3-day scale shift. Your recent carb, creatine, or sodium inputs explain the fluid retention — stay on plan.
copy.honest: Water retention index is sitting at +{biometrics.waterRetentionIndex|int} and the scale is up +{body.weightDeltaKg:3|1dp} kg over three days. It is water chemistry, not tissue gain. Do not slash calories over water.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your water retention index at {biometrics.waterRetentionIndex|int} with a {body.weightDeltaKg:3|abs} kg 3-day drop. Fasting or low carbohydrate turnover has flushed glycogen-bound water — rehydrate and refuel before heavy volume.
copy.honest: Water index is {biometrics.waterRetentionIndex|int} and the scale dropped {body.weightDeltaKg:3|abs} kg in three days. You are depleted of glycogen water. Expect a normal bounce when you eat carbs.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your composite regeneration score down at {biometrics.regenerationScore|int}%. Between CNS load, sleep, and recovery inputs, pushing sets to failure today carries poor return — keep 2–3 reps in reserve.
copy.honest: Regeneration score is {biometrics.regenerationScore|int}%. Grinding max sets today only digs a deeper recovery hole. Train smart at RPE 7 and go to bed early.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your regeneration score at {biometrics.regenerationScore|int}% with {cns.readiness|pct}% CNS readiness. Muscle repair, fuel, and nervous system recovery are aligned — prime window for progressive overload.
copy.honest: {biometrics.regenerationScore|int}% regeneration and {cns.readiness|pct}% CNS readiness. Every physiological light is green today. Put weight on the bar.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Back|int} back sets compared with {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} chest sets this week. Upper-back and lat volume stabilizes your bench and deadlift — add rows or pull-ups.
